author: Torta
subject: Hardcore Rules
content_md:
Hello, weary traveler!

We're excited to unveil a brand-new mode coming to Turtle WoW — one that's not for the faint of heart.

Introducing **Hardcore Mode** — a brutal new way to play, inspired by Diablo's permadeath system and the old-school Hardcore challenges of Classic realms. This is the ultimate test of skill, caution, and sheer stubbornness: level your character to 60 without dying. Not even once.

The ultimate goal of this challenge is to reach level 60 without ever dying. Once you’re level 60, you can participate in raiding and PvP without a risk of losing your character.

To join the challenge, toggle Hardcore Mode when creating your character. While leveling, your character will carry the title **Still Alive**, letting the world know you’re doing it the hard way.

Reach 60 and you'll earn:

- Achievement title **<Immortal>**

- [[Tabard of the Immortal Guardian]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80187)

- [**[Immortal Champion's Charger]**](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80692)

 **Rules [Read it. Live it. Die by it]**

- When your character dies, the game ends for you. If you choose to create and play a hardcore character, you do so at your own risk: we will not restore any deceased hardcore characters for any reason including connection problems, bugs, global warming, your little sister, or any other reason whatsoever.

- Dead characters will remain locked on a selection screen unavailable for playing. As long as you don’t delete them, characters above level 10 will be displayed on our [Scoreboard](https://armory.turtlecraft.gg/hardcore).

- You will be able to trade items and gold only with other Hardcore characters as long as the difference between your levels isn’t higher than 5.

- You will be able to group up only with other Hardcore characters as long as the difference between your levels isn’t higher than 5.

- Hardcore characters can not trade, nor buy on Auction House.

- Hardcore characters can use mail, but with no attachments.

- It is strictly forbidden to multibox if either of your characters is undergoing a Hardcore challenge.

- Hardcore characters are not permitted to get assistance from players outside of their group.

Easy, you lose EXP and de-level or lose your equipment or your spells or your gold. There is a lot of ways to make a Hardcore mode without perma death. Which btw is one of those things that do not really work in WoW(unless you are cheesing it) because of how mob aggro and respawns work.

On that note I think that HC rewards are kinda weak, especially in comparison to turtle mode. I mean the later really just slows you down and gives rewards every 10 levels. HC quite literary cripples your ability to even make gold and its rewards only manifest at 60 and are entirely cosmetic. It could use some basic tweak like for example higher exp rates: you cannot die but you get more exp(something around 1.5-2x rates). Or something along those lines would fit in nicely with the concept of a hardcore mode. The risk is higher but so are the rewards.

On that note I think that HC rewards are kinda weak, especially in comparison to turtle mode. I mean the later really just slows you down and gives rewards every 10 levels. HC quite literary cripples your ability to even make gold and its rewards only manifest at 60 and are entirely cosmetic. It could use some basic tweak like for example higher exp rates: you cannot die but you get more exp(something around 1.5-2x rates). Or something along those lines would fit in nicely with the concept of a hardcore mode. The risk is higher but so are the rewards.

author: Safyre
subject: Re: Hardcore Rules
content_md:
All the restrictions of HC you can put on yourself even without playing HC. But Playing HC keeps everyone honest about it. So if you really don't want perma-death but you want to follow HC restrictions, you can do it. Just do it yourself.

Personally, even though this might defeat the purpose, a few things that might could be considered is:

Decreasing respawn rate in mob crowded areas.
Increasing respawn rate of quest bosses needed to be killed.
Make trading items dependent on the level of the item instead of the level of the character.
Break some of the mob chains so a few mobs can be pulled and not a whole camp.
Not able to cast buffs or heals on PvP flagged individuals (but might not even be possible).
(This one might hurt me) Allow one rez every 15 levels starting at level 15. (gives you 3 lives)

The first five would be really nice and help mend some of the rift between normals and HC. I think not as many HC deaths caused by normals that way. I tend to buff, heal, and help others and sometimes I don't notice they are flagged until it's too late. I haven't actually died to this yet (knocks on wood). The last one is just because $#!+ happens and rezzes are meant for this type of game. But an extreme hard limit on the number of rezzes would be needed. But the caveat for being rezzed is the title of Survivor instead of Immortal. Personally, though, I prefer the one death and done.

The rift between normals and HC that I've experienced is that as a HC, I have to line up my pulls and attacks. Normals don't. This causes me to take a bit longer and while I'm setting up, normals come in and destroy my plans. Then I have to wait for respawn. This can happen over and over. The other thing is normals can pull a bunch and possibly die (or you try to help) and the mobs tag onto the HC while the normal leaves the HC to die.

Because of the things I just mentioned, HC characters tend to wait for normals to thin out areas and then swoop in and grab their targets aggravating the normals. Or HCs just won't help normals because they are afraid they'll get killed. Addressing some of the spawn rates could help these situations... learning MMO etiquette would help too but MMO etiquette has been forgotten since 2010 I think. (grouping with others before pulling a quest mob, waiting your turn when pulling a quest mob if you can't group, noticing that the guy fighting next to a node is clearing the mobs so they can farm that node, etc.)

 -Saf

This causes me to take a bit longer and while I'm setting up, normals come in and destroy my plans. Then I have to wait for respawn. This can happen over and over. The other thing is normals can pull a bunch and possibly die (or you try to help) and the mobs tag onto the HC while the normal leaves the HC to die.

Because of the things I just mentioned, HC characters tend to wait for normals to thin out areas and then swoop in and grab their targets aggravating the normals. Or HCs just won't help normals because they are afraid they'll get killed. Addressing some of the spawn rates could help these situations... learning MMO etiquette would help too but MMO etiquette has been forgotten since 2010 I think. (grouping with others before pulling a quest mob, waiting your turn when pulling a quest mob if you can't group, noticing that the guy fighting next to a node is clearing the mobs so they can farm that node, etc.)

-Saf

HC characters should be protected from disconnects both client- and server-side. Something like Ascension does, where characters are teleported to a safe zone in case of disconnects. I love this server and appreciate the work that was put in, but HC challenge should be about skill and adventure, not server infrastructure. You killed my motivation to play HC and Turtle Wow, and I am not getting back unless HC challenge will get updated. I will follow the development of the server, but you lost a loyal player for now (and most likely many others, who enjoyed HC and quit, because of strict rules).

author: Jolikmc
subject: Re: Hardcore Rules
content_md:
It baffles me that people want "insurance" for their "all-or-nothing" characters.  Is it really so hard to just, you know, take the necessary precautions before attempting to play a Hardcore character?

I realize that accidents happen.  Sometimes, the server goes down at an inopportune time.  Sometimes, so does your local Internet.  Occasionally, you might get a bad pull.  Maybe you even managed to get yourself flagged by trying to be a Good Samaritan.  Well… those are the risks you take.

Let's say you decide to go mountain climbing in real life.  You check your equipment twice, make sure you have someone with you, and all that.  Well, let's say that despite everything, you manage to hook onto a loose bit of cliff and end up falling to your death.  Did you know that was going to happen for certain?  Of course not.  Did you figure that it was always a possibility?  More than likely.  But, you still went ahead and went mountain climbing for whatever reason.
Same thing applies to Hardcore.  It's a choice you make.  When you make your choice, you need to accept whatever comes with that choice.  Otherwise, what's the point?  You may as well just play a normal character and do an "honor system" Hardcore run.  Sure, you won't get any prizes for hitting Level 60 with 0 deaths, but you can still take a screenshot and brag to your guild about it.

I dunno.  Maybe I'm completely wrong, here.  It just seems counter-productive to have a "no death" mode, but then have an "redo" in case you die anyway.

You may as well just play a normal character and do an "honor system" Hardcore run. I dunno. Maybe I'm completely wrong, here. It just seems counter-productive to have a "no death" mode, but then have an "redo" in case you die anyway.

I understand that some people enjoy relevelling when they die due to DC, but I would guess the server loses a lot of HC characters by not even trying to make the experience more about the skill and less about everything else.

You can be of your opinion, where you just say "death is death" and we do not care about the rest. Or you can be of opinion that hardcore challenge is a challenge/experience for players to enjoy, and therefore, the point of the server is to make this experience nice for the players without reducing the actual challenge.

author: Grantgrace
subject: Re: Depression
content_md:
Losing a character you've invested time and emotion into can feel like a real blow. It's natural to feel down, and even if you're surrounded by people, that sense of loneliness can still creep in. What I've found helpful is talking about it with fellow gamers who've been through similar experiences. Sharing stories and strategies for coping can make you feel understood and less alone.
Remember, there's no shame in reaching out for support. Sometimes, a [hotline for mental health](https://mentalhealthhotline.org/) can provide valuable advice and someone to listen to when you're navigating tough emotions. Taking care of your mental well-being is crucial, both inside the game and in your day-to-day life.

This isn't something we want to implement currently, sorry.

I see there is an underlying risk that should be mitigated as it would potentially lead to some downsides for us Turtles. However, why can't we explore this idea a bit further to weigh off good and bad? Maybe we can accommodate for the downsides if it means more upside on the other hand? One common fallacy in modern businesses to avoid is also that adding new features isn't the only thing or even always recommended. Some development should always be dedicated to improve the existing experience.

I also want to highlight that **enabling PvP is a feature request at the heart of many players** and if we look at it from a strategic lens it would for example give Turtle WoW even more of an edge against others who provide the Hardcore experience.

In the Hardcore challenge we set out to challenge the PvE environment in quests, open world and dungeons. While I understand there are more challenges involved to make PvP available in the open world, I see a much lower hanging fruit in enabling it for battlegrounds.

 **So what does it really mean for us to explore** (incomplete list):

Assumptions to check with Dev-Team for tech. feasibility
 - Can we disable Hardcore in Battlegrounds or add a temporary condition to make players revivable?
 - Can we access the code that causes players to be flagged for PvP after a battleground?
 - Can we touch this code safely or is there any possibility of a workaround?
 - Can we use the event of leaving the Battleground to trigger another event like a buff similar to desertion?
 - Can we protect Hardcore players in the event of them leaving the Battleground with a protection buff?
 - Can we make this buff/debuff exclusive to outside of battlegrounds?
 - Can we test this live with a disclaimer or an otherwise safe environment?
 - ..

Hardcore pinciples & ethics to explore
 - Isn't Hardcore more of a PvE experience and we should look at PvP from a separate lens?
 - Is there any usecase for Hardcore being enabled in Battlegrounds that is actively practiced? Is it worth overruling it or a possibility to stay mortal in battlegrounds?
 - Does never dieing in an instance specifically intended for PvP as a game mode really go against the Hardcore ethos that is more PvE focused?
 - What would be the impact on the Battleground & Hardcore Experience for players in various modes alike?
 - ..

Also here an example worth considering: Currently Hardcore players negatively influence the Battleground Experience for normal players in the 10-19 bracket with quests like Horde Defender Axe. Finding a way to accommodate would serve both sides.

Feel free to add any more angles or ideas to explore the possibility of providing accessibility to Battlegrounds for Hardcore players.

Personally, I'd be delighted if this can be implemented as I follow somewhat a completionist approach to Hardcore and also love to engage in Player vs Player.

Thanks for your consideration and bringing this thread to the attention of the Turtle WoW Team, specifically Product Management and Engineering.

author: InfernoTooFewPlayers
subject: Hardcore should be permanent for all even when you reach 60
content_md:
I really enjoyed playing hardcore and I would consider supporting this project more if something was done about lack of players on inferno. Finding a group for dungeons becomes impossible when playing inferno and I have stopped playing as I cant find any players for dungeons.

Different suggestions how to fix lack of players on inferno:

a) **Merge Nordanaar and Telabim servers.** There are not many inferno players on Telabim (sorry if I don't got the server names right) but the few players there would unite the community if servers merged.

b) **Players who choose hardcore should no longer get the title immortal and mount at lvl 60, instead hardcore is permanent even when you reach lvl 60.** You can remove the "inferno" and simply call it hardcore. (This is the most important suggestion which should be done!)

c) **Make it easier and faster to go from hardcore to inferno.** I don't understand why you added extra steps which cannot be soloed to play inferno. This reduces the number of players who play hardcore at lvl 60 since the quest to become inferno is complicated for new players as you don't know if you are permanent hardcore or not (go to a mailbox below karazhan guarded by 20 lvl 60 mobs which just drags it out. Players wanna do dungeons, raids and other fun stuff instead of trying to get to a mailbox and escorting new players there).

d) **Remove level restrictions for trading and mailing items due to trade chain exploit.** If you create alts and level them up you can trade with anyone and it becomes a chore. Its hard to sell and buy items since there basically is no market. Keep the AH closed for hardcore, but enable only trading and mail. This means level 60s will be able to give petri flasks for low levels but it will increase number of players who are willing to play hardcore and inferno.

e) **Hide the dungeon finder icon when playing hardcore.** This is confusing for many players as to why it doesnt work when it is infact disabled in hardcore mode.

f) **Add stats how many succesful dungeons a player has completed when you shift-click a players name in chat.** This will allow experienced pug players to be trusted by guilds to play more together. Currently many guilds will only play dungeons with guildies because they think pugs are inexperienced and dont know how to pull packs, boss encounters, gear etc.

g) **Dire Maul should be 5 players max, and not possible to do 10 player raid.** As a tank it's hard to find a group for dungeons due to this, due to only needing 1 tank for 10 man raids in 5 man dungeons, it also becomes too easy removing the otherwise awesome feeling when playing hardcore.

h) **Hardcore players should not be able to create portable banks, mailboxes and repair bots which follow you.** This makes the game simply too easy and not "hardcore".

i) **Make the challenges in character creation screen bigger and easier to find.**  Many players dont know there is in fact challenges such as hardcore mode when you create your character as it is easy to miss the button that opens the submenu for it.

author: Sigune
subject: Re: Warrior or Rogue
content_md:
> **Brom wrote: Mon May 19, 2025 3:29 pm**
> Hey guys.
>  I hear people talking all the time about how the warrior is the hardest class for HC. But what about the rogue? I've no experience as a rogue but i think they are too a melee one x one class and must be squishier than a warrior. Right?
>  Why is the warrior considered worst than the rogue for HC? What is the rogue advantage over the warrior?

As the person who has both an immortal warrior and an immortal rogue I can confidently say: rogue is way easier than warrior.

Rogue has a ton of options to escape, warrior only has intimidating shout pretty much. Retaliation can help you to survive a tricky situation by standing your ground, but sometimes you just **have** to run. Got cornered by undeads that are immune to fear, and retaliation is still on cooldown? Time to think about your next character's name.

Next, Rogue is way less gear reliant than warrior. Well, if you spec into combat that's true, so make an Ambush build instead. You are going to crit for half of the mob health from Ambush with 100% crit chance due to the Remorseless Attacks and Improved Ambush talents. I am currently leveling a vagrant artisan rogue with level 5 copper daggers as my main weapons, and this build is still going strong at level 53, albeit it removes ~20% and not ~50% on Ambush crit at this level.

Of course, Rogue is not an auto win button. They are indeed squishy, that's true. If you want an auto win melee class, you should probably roll paladin. Rogues are also susceptible to hubris (I can stealth though those dense packs of elites no problems!..), but way less so than hunters and warlocks. And be wary that you can also screw yourself up royally if you place target dummy then vanish, that's a bad idea. For rogue, pick alchemy+herbalism instead.

Once you get to level 22 as rogue and get Vanish, you are set to success. Before that, be super careful.
And don't do your poison class quest before you get Vanish.
Hope that helps~

author: Winthrop
subject: Re: Slow HC Artisan
content_md:
So Im playing those challenges(hc, SnS, Artisan) + exhaustion as a frostmage, currently level 47.

I started with mining & Skinning up to Bronze(Loch Modan).
Then took JC to craft the best Ring(Trainer), neck(Trainer), Staff(Serpentcoil world drop recipe) and Trinket (shadoweye farmable in Loch Modan)

In the meantime I sold leather for Gold then switched to Tailoring. You will have lots of wool from the Shadoweye farm.
This means you will be running around for quiet a while without clothing.

From there on full invest in Tailor & Enchanting.

Great thing about the wetlands is the silkbolts you get through fishing!
Don't skip out on cooking for the juicy mp5 sagefish caught in Loch Modan.

Been a blast so far! Enjoy the journey.

Yes, the challenge ends when you reach level 60.

This quest is available from level 55, and you must complete it before reaching level 60.

author: Hypaethralfm
subject: HC leveling static
content_md:
[Update 12/12] Full :)
[Update 12/10] we're interested in also adding slow & steady given we want to explore and don't want to dungeon spam anyway
[Update 12/10] 1 slot left!  Thanks for the interest so far :)

Hello there!

We are a group of three new to turtlewow who are excited to form a static leveling group for hardcore 1-60. Currently have two slots! Ideally we'd only play these characters together from about level 6 or so (enough to make it to a shared leveling zone).  We'd like individual deaths to be counted as full-group deaths: if one goes of us goes down, we all restart together!  We're also enabling the 'no rested XP' challenge and aim to do a healthy mix of dungeon and overworld content for leveling.  At the moment we don't plan to get into inferno (where you permanently stay HC after hitting 60) or really much raiding, so most likely it'd be a one-off leveling experience with endgame tapering off at the end. Gaming is our main hobby, we're all a little goofy, and we have very flexible USA evening hours :)

If leveling as a static and hanging out sounds fun to you, feel free to share your interest either here or on add on disc ( t.ai )

Generally would be keen to know three things:
 - general mindset / expectations, just a brief intro would be plenty!
 - class/role interest
 - general availability

Stay gaming   smiling_turtle

author: Drakz
subject: A suggestion about HC deaths
content_md:
Hey everyone,

I just wanted to bring up an issue that’s been really frustrating for a lot of us in the Hardcore community. A lot of deaths lately aren’t coming from gameplay mistakes - they’re happening because of server disconnects, like the one on January 20th at 10:50 PM EET.

I think it would be a really good idea for the server to consider doing a small rollback in situations like this. Losing progress or characters due to issues completely outside of our control is super frustrating and honestly risks losing part of the playerbase.

Also, I’ve noticed some moderators on Discord blaming players for these deaths, even though it’s obvious we were all disconnected at the same time from different countries. It’s disheartening to be accused when it’s clearly a server problem.

I hope this can be considered seriously - it would make the Hardcore experience much less stressful and more fair.

Thanks for reading.

author: Sleeplust
subject: Re: A suggestion about HC deaths
content_md:
The core debate is whether our hardcore gaming should count server restarts and disconnection in as "regular" part of the game.

As some players claim, everything, including every incident like real-life wars, server crashes, game glithes and earthquakes should not be reasons for HC absolution. Even if other players think characters in game who die for those issues should be revived or reclaimed, the biggest question lies in how to identify those issues in order to prevent the mechanism being abused. If it is abused, GMs' workload and further complaints may also multiply because every player may say that server latency ruins his character.

My compromised suggestion is having dead HC characters moved and revived in a less active or unpopular realm/server, such as current PVP servers in Feb. 2026, as non-HC ones, which would compensate the players' dedication and help people stay in the game. Despite the frustration, they don't feel completely lost as their life, time and energy are not pathetically wasted.

Other than that, as TWoW's HC mode isn't Blizzard's HC servers, there have been several specific functions implemented, including preventing unwanted PVP engages. I think HC characters should be tagged for more such mechanisms, such as automatically teleporting them to an inn when the server restarts without warning. Such restarts typically occur with a rollback, so characters may find themselves among respawned mobs.

author: Kefke
subject: Re: Died from a scripted quest
content_md:
Bottom feeders getting their joy from the misery of others aside, I feel your pain. The quest is infamous for a reason. A lot of us know about it because of that, but I can understand not wanting to research every step of your journey. People play HC for different reasons, and carefully planning out the safest route possible to eliminate risk is just not going to be how everyone wants to play.

And to be honest, I don't think it's that unreasonable to think a change should be made. When the original devs made game, death was an expected and semi-trivial part of the gameplay loop. You drink the potion, you'd die, you'd do the objective and respawn. The quest was not designed with the idea that players would be doing deathless runs. Even if the Turtle devs don't want to add an exception to the enforced hardcore mechanics, I think that slapping a warning label of "THIS WILL KILL YOUR CHARACTER" on the quest for people who haven't heard of it in advance is pretty reasonable. There's a mechanical consequence attached, enforced by the game, that wasn't there when the quest was made.

author: Daoc2001
subject: Re: Died from a scripted quest
content_md:
I've leveled multiple HC characters to 60 on Nord & Amber simply to make things a bit more tense & unpredictable during the 1-60 journey, but it really does go (often painfully) against the fundamental design of the WoW game - & Turtle WoW Devs haven't done much of anything to incorporate it properly.

Crafting can especially be a huge headache for obtaining certain other-profession-only crafted ingredients that you will need without the AH.  And, HC channel is basically useless outside of socially-challenged HC players trolling one another.  Even in one of the large HC guilds, you will often find yourself hawking the guild channel for days/weeks randomly  just to get basic crafting ingredients only available from other crafting professions from someone within 5 levels of yourself.  I've learned to just ignore crafting professions altogether until you hit 60 while HC & can finally use the AH as an Immortal "Normie".

So, "buyer beware" if choosing Turtle WoW HC play for whatever reason you are choosing to go that route.

author: Springboards
subject: Re: Rare monsters
content_md: Rare monsters nearly always did insane damage for their level-- while having a low healthpool( almost as much as a standard mob their own lvl), they compensated for that by having extreme dps. This is very easily to check with wowvanilladb--> for example it lists foe reaper(lvl 20) <https://classicdb.ch/?npc=573> having 148-175 avg dmg, which is insane for its level; most characters have about 250-300 hp at that point. It doesnt get any better--e.g, for example <https://classicdb.ch/?npc=14229> accursed slitherblade lvl 36 normal rare does a whooping 356-384 dmg per swing before any crits. always be careful , check wowvanilladb for their dmg range and abilites if you are not sure, there is also a rare in darkshore which has thrash and mob thrash is 2! extra attacks, not one, so be prepared to get hit for 3 attacks for  156 - 186 dmg from a lvl 16. I dont think many characters at lvl 16 can take such an attack.

author: Rejuve
subject: Red & Orange
content_md:
There is a challenge that allows the hc char to only get XP from R&O quests, and certain level mobs.

Compared to what is the case in ordinary hc play I feel this challenge is unnecessarily hard/slow.
OR, that there is a missing challenge in between.

One step up from ordinary hc play should be to only gain xp from yellow+ quests (or even abit easier).
The level number on the mobs/quests can be used too, that u only gain xp from mobs 1 level below ure char and up.

AND, I think this/these challenges should award something substantial at 60. I dont know what it should be, free ports everywhere or other stuff.

All this because I think the idea with this type of challenge is really interesting.

author: Rejuve
subject: Cap HC-guilds at max 50 or 100 players !
content_md:
I wrote players and not chars, since it is possible for one and same player to have more hc-chars but only be counted as one player in a guild. And it is possible for Turtle to programme this.

A large portion of the hc chars on Ambershire realm are in guilds HC Heroes or Only Once, instead of being spread around in smaller guilds. Those guilds are huge, like 1000 players in each guild. They are like the giant concrete bus-stations of Hamburg and Munich. They are there mostly because of lacking world-chat/trade hc channels made by Turtle. There is no enthusiasm in their guild chat, because they are strangers to each other, and as player they cant really make a difference regarding anything in their guild.

The guild scene on a server should crawl with many different guild-names. There should be rivalry, drama-talk, praising etc in chats, not the dead, empty, hollow stuff we have on Ambershire today. The social scene is dead boring now !
